template.name: AI Governance Maturity Self-Assessment
template.disclaimer: This self-assessment produces an indicative, self-reported view of AI governance maturity. All results are User-asserted: no evidence has been reviewed. Framework readiness indicators are not a determination of conformity with ISO/IEC 42001, compliance with the EU AI Act, or alignment with NIST AI RMF. VERITRAIL does not certify compliance and this report is not legal advice.

scale.label: Initial / ad hoc
scale.description: Practice exists informally or in pockets; not documented or repeatable.

scale.label: Defined for some systems
scale.description: Documented practice applied to some systems or business units.

scale.label: Consistently implemented
scale.description: Practice applied consistently across material AI systems with records.

scale.label: Measured, automated, and continuously improved
scale.description: Practice is measured, largely automated and improved from metrics.

levels.name: Initial
levels.interpretation: AI governance is ad hoc; immediate foundational work required.

levels.name: Developing
levels.interpretation: Basic practices exist but are inconsistent and hard to evidence.

levels.name: Defined
levels.interpretation: Core governance is established; expand coverage and automation.

levels.name: Managed
levels.interpretation: Controls are monitored and integrated into operations.

levels.name: Optimized
levels.interpretation: Governance is adaptive, automated and continuously assured.

profile_fields.label: Approximate number of AI systems in use
Do you use AI agents or autonomous workflows?
Do you place AI on the EU market or use AI affecting people in the EU?

questions.text: Does your organization have a documented AI governance policy and accountable ownership model?
questions.action: Approve and publish an AI governance policy with a named executive owner and accountability model.

questions.text: Is there a cross-functional AI governance forum with authority to approve, restrict, or stop AI use cases?
questions.action: Charter a cross-functional AI governance forum with documented authority to approve, restrict or stop use cases.

questions.text: Are AI roles, responsibilities, and escalation paths defined for business, technology, risk, legal, and security teams?
questions.action: Publish an AI RACI and escalation matrix covering business, technology, risk, legal, privacy and security.

questions.text: Does your organization maintain a complete inventory of AI systems, models, agents, and vendor AI products?
questions.action: Stand up an AI system of record and run inventory workshops plus shadow-AI discovery to reach full coverage.

questions.text: Are AI systems classified by business criticality, data sensitivity, decision impact, autonomy, and regulatory relevance?
questions.action: Apply VERITRAIL risk-tier criteria to every inventory record and approve tier assignments.

questions.text: Can you identify the owner, purpose, users, data sources, and dependencies for each material AI system?
questions.action: Complete owner, purpose, users, data-source and dependency fields for all material AI systems.

questions.text: Do AI use cases undergo risk assessment before production deployment?
questions.action: Make a tier-proportionate risk and impact assessment a mandatory gate before any production deployment.

questions.text: Are model, prompt, data, vendor, and agent changes subject to change control and reassessment?
questions.action: Add AI-specific change triggers (model, prompt, data, vendor, tool, agent) to change management with reassessment rules.

questions.text: Is there a defined process for retiring, restricting, or remediating AI systems that no longer meet requirements?
questions.action: Define restrict/remediate/retire procedures and an exception register with expiry dates.

questions.text: Are data sources, data classifications, and data flows documented for AI systems?
questions.action: Document data sources, classifications and data flows for each material AI system.

questions.text: Are privacy, consent, retention, cross-border transfer, and data-minimization requirements assessed?
questions.action: Embed privacy impact assessment (consent, retention, transfers, minimisation) into AI intake and change.

questions.text: Are sensitive data fields redacted, masked, or excluded from prompts, logs, and external model calls?
questions.action: Deploy redaction/masking for prompts, responses, logs and external model calls, starting with highest-sensitivity systems.

questions.text: Are AI systems included in threat modeling, security review, and vulnerability-management processes?
questions.action: Extend threat modelling, security review and vulnerability management to all AI systems and model supply chains.

questions.text: Are LLM applications and agents tested for prompt injection, jailbreak, data leakage, and unsafe tool use?
questions.action: Run adversarial testing (prompt injection, jailbreak, leakage, unsafe tool use) before release and after material change.

questions.text: Can you disable or roll back an AI system, model, agent, or tool quickly after a security or safety incident?
questions.action: Implement and test a kill switch and rollback runbook for every production AI system and agent.

questions.text: Are AI systems assessed for bias, discriminatory outcomes, safety risks, and unintended harm?
questions.action: Introduce bias, safety and harm evaluation for high-impact systems with documented thresholds.

questions.text: Are users informed when they are interacting with AI or when AI materially influences a decision?
questions.action: Standardise AI disclosures for AI interactions and AI-influenced decisions.

questions.text: Are explanations, disclosures, and appeal mechanisms available for affected individuals where appropriate?
questions.action: Provide explanation and appeal routes for individuals affected by AI-influenced decisions.

questions.text: Are human-review, override, escalation, and appeal mechanisms defined for high-impact AI decisions?
questions.action: Define human review, override and approval points for high-impact AI decisions and agent actions.

questions.text: Are AI systems monitored for performance, drift, misuse, incidents, and unexpected behavior?
questions.action: Instrument production AI for performance, drift, misuse and incident monitoring with alert thresholds.

questions.text: Are operators and affected teams trained on AI limitations, escalation paths, and responsible use?
questions.action: Roll out role-based AI literacy and operator training with completion tracking.

questions.text: Are AI controls tested periodically, with evidence retained for audit and review?
questions.action: Establish a periodic AI control-testing programme with an evidence repository and retention rules.

questions.text: Can your organization produce an audit-ready evidence pack for a material AI system on request?
questions.action: Build an audit-ready evidence pack for your highest-risk AI system and template it for the rest.

questions.text: Are AI governance metrics reviewed by leadership and used to drive corrective action?
questions.action: Define AI governance KPIs and review them in a recurring leadership forum with tracked corrective actions.

critical_flags.title: No reliable AI inventory
critical_flags.rationale: Without a complete inventory, risk tiering, oversight and evidence cannot be applied to systems you do not know about.

critical_flags.title: AI deployed without pre-deployment risk assessment
critical_flags.rationale: Systems reaching production without risk assessment may carry unidentified legal, safety or security exposure.

critical_flags.title: Sensitive data may reach prompts, logs or external models
critical_flags.rationale: Unredacted personal or confidential data in prompts and logs creates privacy and confidentiality exposure.

critical_flags.title: Agents or LLM apps not tested for prompt injection and unsafe tool use
critical_flags.rationale: Agents with tool access that are untested for injection can be manipulated into unauthorised actions or data leakage.

critical_flags.title: No tested kill switch or rollback
critical_flags.rationale: Without containment, an AI incident cannot be stopped quickly.

critical_flags.title: High-impact decisions lack defined human oversight
critical_flags.rationale: High-impact AI decisions without review, override or appeal raise fairness, safety and accountability exposure.

critical_flags.title: Cannot produce audit-ready evidence
critical_flags.rationale: Inability to evidence controls undermines responses to auditors, customers and regulators.

critical_flags.title: EU-facing AI without consistent AI-interaction disclosure
critical_flags.rationale: Transparency obligations for certain AI systems (EU AI Act Art. 50) require readiness; legal review recommended.

critical_flags.title: No AI governance policy or accountable owner
critical_flags.rationale: Without a policy and owner, no one is accountable for AI risk decisions.

### First 30 days — stabilise

- Document data sources, classifications and data flows for each material AI system. (Data & Privacy; DAT-Q1; controls EI-06, IS-02)
- Embed privacy impact assessment (consent, retention, transfers, minimisation) into AI intake and change. (Data & Privacy; DAT-Q2; controls IS-03)

### Days 61–90 — scale and automate

- Apply VERITRAIL risk-tier criteria to every inventory record and approve tier assignments. (AI Inventory & Visibility; INV-Q2; controls EI-02)
- Extend threat modelling, security review and vulnerability management to all AI systems and model supply chains. (Security & Resilience; SEC-Q1; controls IS-01, IS-10)
- Publish an AI RACI and escalation matrix covering business, technology, risk, legal, privacy and security. (Strategy & Accountability; STR-Q3; controls AO-03, AO-06)
- Deploy redaction/masking for prompts, responses, logs and external model calls, starting with highest-sensitivity systems. (Data & Privacy; DAT-Q3; controls IS-04)
